::: {.column width="40%"}
##### Pre-Processing

1.  Remove vacant buildings.
2.  Remove Hawaii & Alaska.
3.  Remove households with no Air-Conditioning OR unavailable Air-Conditioning.
4.  Randomly remove **20%** of observations in each climate region for model testing purposes

## Models Under Evaluation {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
##### Models

```{r}
#| label: 'Model Eval Table'
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: '*Approach drawn from Zhang, Robinson, et. al. (2018): Estimating Residential Energy Consumption in Metropolitan Areas: A Microsimulation Approach*'




model_candidates |> 
  mutate(
    link_text = str_extract(technical_details, "details_(.+)\\.html", group = 1),  # extracts "linear_reg_lm"
    technical_details = str_glue('<a href="{technical_details}" target="_blank">{link_text}</a>')
  ) |> 
  select(-link_text, -underlying_engine) |>  
  rename(Model = model_type, `{Parsnip} Details` = technical_details) |> 
  tinytable::tt() |> 
  tinytable::theme_html(class = "tinytable tinytable-striped")

```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
##### Evaluation Metrics

1.  **R-Squared:** How much variation in cooling load does our model explain?
    -   $$
        R^2 = 1 - \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2}{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i - \bar{y})^2} = 1 - \frac{SS_{res}}{SS_{tot}}
        $$
2.  **Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE):** On average, how far off is predicted cooling load from observed cooling load?
    -   $$
        RMSE = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2}
        $$
:::
:::::

## Resampling: 10-Fold Cross Validation {.smaller}

:::::: columns
:::: column
<!-- ![](helper_files/cfv_exp.png) -->

<!-- *Taken from [Tidy Modeling with R](https://www.tmwr.org/)* -->

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "*Image recreated from [Tidy Modeling with R](https://www.tmwr.org/)*"

flowchart TD
    AllData((All Data))
    Training[Training]
    Testing[Testing]
    
    AllData --> Training
    AllData --> Testing
    
    R1[Resample 1]
    R2[Resample 2]
    Dots[...]
    RB[Resample B]
    
    Training --> R1
    Training --> R2
    Training --> Dots
    Training --> RB
    
    R1 --> A1([Analysis])
    R1 --> As1([Assessment])
    R2 --> A2([Analysis])
    R2 --> As2([Assessment])
    RB --> AB([Analysis])
    RB --> AsB([Assessment])
    
    classDef trainingStyle fill:#f5deb3,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    classDef testingStyle fill:#e6e6fa,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    classDef neutralStyle fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    
    class Training,A1,A2,AB trainingStyle
    class Testing,As1,As2,AsB testingStyle
    class R1,R2,RB,Dots neutralStyle
```

::: callout-tip
## What's the Point?

1.  Helps assess how well your model will handle unseen or out of sample data
2.  Stabilizes evaluation and performance metrics by averaging them across K-Folds
3.  Partitions data so that you never test on the same data that you train
4.  Helps detect possible over-fitting, especially in higher variance models
:::
::::

::: column

# Optimizing Xgboost

## Parameter Tuning {.smaller}


:::::: columns
::: column
### `{xgboost}: Defaults`

```{r}
#| label: 'xgboost args'
#| eval: false
#| echo: true 

## Xgboost defaults | What I relied on in the initial CFV evaluation
xgboost =
   boost_tree(
      mode = "regression",           
      engine = "xgboost",           
      mtry = NULL,              # Number of predictors randomly sampled at each split (Everything by default)
      trees = NULL,             # Number of boosting iterations (10 by default)
      min_n = NULL,             # Min data points in node required to split (1 by default) 
      tree_depth = NULL,        # Max depth of each tree (6 by default)
      learn_rate = NULL,        # Shrinkage (eta): how much each tree contributes (.3 by default)
      loss_reduction = NULL,    # Min loss reduction (gamma) required to split (0 by default)
      sample_size = NULL,       # Proportion of data sampled for each tree (1 by default | Whole sample)
      stop_iter = NULL          # Early stopping: iterations without improvement (No stopping by default)
      
)
```
:::

::: column
::: callout-tip
## The Concept

"These fancier machine learning algorithms have tuning parameters that control their fitting behavior. Because we don't know the **optimal values ahead of time, we test different combinations to find what works best.** "
:::
:::
::::::


##  Parameter Tuning {.smaller}



:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column}

```{r}
#| include: false


mixed_humid_exp <-
  dbGetQuery(con, 'SELECT * FROM train."4A"') |>
  as_tibble()



```

### `{xgboost}: Tuning Specification`
```{r}
#| label: 'xgboost tuning example'
#| echo: true

## Anchor randomization
set.seed(1 - 25 - 2026)

## Tell R what I want to tune 
xgb_spec <-
  boost_tree(
    mode = "regression",
    engine = "xgboost",
    mtry = tune(),
    trees = 1000,
    min_n = tune(),
    tree_depth = tune(),
    learn_rate = tune(),
    loss_reduction = tune(),
    sample_size = tune(),
    stop_iter = 10
  )

## Populate a grid with latin hypercube sampling 
xgb_grid <- 
  grid_space_filling(
    finalize(mtry(), mixed_humid_exp),
    min_n(),
    tree_depth(),
    learn_rate(),
    loss_reduction(),
    sample_size = sample_prop(),
    size = 30,
    type = "latin_hypercube",
    original = TRUE
  )

```
:::


::: {.column}

#| label: 'make param tuning graphs'

r2_param_labs <-
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = 'Mean R2 Over 10-Fold CFV'
  )

r2_params_plots <-
  r2_params_viz |>
  ggplot(aes(
    param_combos,
    mean,
    color = benchmark_helper,
    alpha = benchmark_helper
  )) +
  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(
      tooltip = str_glue(
        "mtry: {mtry}
min_n: {min_n}
tree_depth: {tree_depth}
learn_rate: {learn_rate}
loss_reduction: {loss_reduction}
sample_size: {sample_size}
Mean R²: {round(mean, 3)}"
      )
    ),
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = default_r2_benchmark,
    linetype = 'dashed',
    color = 'red'
  ) +
  annotate(
    'text',
    x = 30,
    y = default_r2_benchmark - .05,
    label = str_glue('Default Benchmark: {round(default_r2_benchmark, 2)}'),
    hjust = .1,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(.25, 1.25)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c('gray', '#807DBA')) +
  coord_flip() +
  r2_param_labs +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent"),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "transparent"),
     plot.title = element_markdown(hjust = .5),
    plot.subtitel = element_markdown(hjust = .5),
    legend.position = 'none',
    text = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text.y = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10))
  )


rmse_param_labs <-
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = 'Mean RMSE Over 10-Fold CFV'
  )

rmse_params_plots <-
  rmse_params_viz |>
  ggplot(aes(
    param_combos,
    mean,
    color = benchmark_helper,
    alpha = benchmark_helper
  )) +
  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(
      tooltip = str_glue(
        "mtry: {mtry}
min_n: {min_n}
tree_depth: {tree_depth}
learn_rate: {learn_rate}
loss_reduction: {loss_reduction}
sample_size: {sample_size}
Mean R²: {round(mean, 3)}"
      )
    ),
    size = 3
  ) + # Removed color = '#807DBA' to respect the aes mapping
  geom_hline(
